question: Why does the curse of dimensionality motivate dimensionality reduction?
direct_answer: Because high-dimensional data become sparse, making distance and density-based reasoning harder.
expanded_answer: As dimensionality grows, the available space expands very quickly, so data points occupy only a tiny fraction of it unless you have enormous data. This sparsity weakens nearest-neighbor methods, density estimation, and some generalization behavior because distances become less informative.
key_points: Data become sparse in the ambient space
common_wrong_ideas: More dimensions always mean more information
Curse of dimensionality only matters for images
Distance-based methods are unaffected by dimension
